claim: Jay Clayton spent more than twenty years at the Wall Street law firm Sullivan & Cromwell — the firm the Dulles brothers once ran — where he was co-managing partner of its General Practice Group, before chairing the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the federal markets regulator, from May 2017 to December 2020. In February 2021 Apollo Global Management named him lead independent director, and on March 22, 2021 he became non-executive chairman of Apollo's board, succeeding founder Leon Black — who had stepped down after an Apollo-commissioned review found he paid Jeffrey Epstein $158 million between 2012 and 2017 for tax and estate advice. In 2025 Clayton became U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York (SDNY), the office that prosecuted Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell and that holds the case files. A U.S. Department of Justice news briefing in the federal Epstein release records that, at President Trump's urging, Attorney General Pam Bondi directed Clayton to investigate Epstein's ties to Trump's political opponents — placing the disposition of the Epstein files with a Sullivan & Cromwell alumnus who had chaired the SEC and then the board seat vacated over Epstein payments.
